newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pollster sees left winning second round.
newsitem.headline: French pollster sees left winning second round.

text.p: A coalition of left-wing parties is likely to win the second round of France's parliamentary election next Sunday and obtain a majority in the National Assembly, a leading pollster said on Monday.

CSA Institute Political Director Roland Cayrol said in most cases French people confirmed in the second round their first round voting trends. But he added the ruling centre-right coalition could still pull off a close win next Sunday.

"We have a two-thirds possibility that the Socialists will confirm their victory next Sunday but there is a one-third possibility that there is a reverse current," Cayrol told Reuters Financial Television.
Cayrol said President Jacques Chirac's centre-right faced a tough fight to reverse Sunday's lead for the combined left.
"It will be very hard, Mr Chirac will have to prove he personally wants to fight for the election. He has to prove it is a personal thing for him," he said.

"He is the only one within the majority who is able to reverse the current, so if Mr Chirac wants to play a personal involvement in the election, if he wants to prove that he will not keep Mr (Alain) Juppe as the prime minister, that he will have a new team for a new policy then maybe it is possible," Cayrol said.
The left's first round win was probably a surprise to French voters, he said.
"When we asked them about their prognosis before the election, five people out of six said they envisaged an easy victory for the right," Cayrol said.

He said the result was in line with past electoral behaviour in France where in each general elections, whether parliamentary or presidential, voters have used their ballots to sanction the previous government.
He added that the extreme-right National Front led by Jean-Marie Lepen, which polled about 15 percent in the first round, was now a force to contend with in all French elections.
The Front would try to act as arbiter between right and left in about 100 constituencies where its candidates made a strong enough showing to stand in the second round, he said.
